messages:
Eli (Eng): Hi @people-ops — quick question. My spouse just accepted a job and their benefits start next month. I want to remove them from our plan to avoid double premiums. Is that considered a QLE and how tight are the timelines?
Nora (People Ops): Congrats to your spouse! Yes, gaining other employer coverage is a recognized QLE (loss/gain of other coverage depending on carrier rules). You typically have 30 days from the event (the spouses new coverage effective date) to make the change. Do you know their official start/effective date?
Eli (Eng): Effective 2025-11-01 per their HR letter. Theyre covered from their first day.
Kai (Benefits): On our side carriers usually accept "gain of other coverage" as a QLE if you provide one of: 1) employer coverage letter showing effective date, 2) benefits confirmation email, or 3) paystub showing deductions. Upload whichever is easiest.
Eli (Eng): If I drop spouse, when does payroll stop charging me for the dependent coverage? Is it immediate or proration happens?
Kai (Benefits): Good question. Coverage termination date typically aligns with the QLE effective date (spouses coverage start). Payroll will prorate premiums if the change falls within a payroll period. Example: if your payroll runs biweekly and the dependent coverage ends mid-period, payroll calculates pro-rated premium and processes a refund or reduces the upcoming deduction. PayrollBot will show the adjustment amount.
Eli (Eng): Will there be any retro adjustments if I forget to submit on time? What if I miss the 30-day window?
Nora (People Ops): If you enroll/terminate outside the 30-day window, it becomes an open enrollment-only change unless you request an exception. Exceptions for late QLE are rare but possible with proof showing administrative delay on the spouses side (e.g., HR letter issued late). If we approve a late QLE, payroll retro-adjustment may apply back to the QLE effective date, but approvals are on a case-by-case basis.
Eli (Eng): And HSA contributions? If I drop spouse mid-year and switch to employee-only HDHP, do I need to change my HSA election too?
Kai (Benefits): Yes — HSA election is tied to coverage tier. If you move from family to individual HDHP mid-year, you should update your HSA contribution. Employer contribution proration rules apply. Note: If you contributed more than the IRS pro-rated family limit during the portion of the year you had family coverage, you may need to correct via distribution or return of excess. We recommend speaking with benefits/tax advisor if you're near contribution limits.
Eli (Eng): Any docs I should upload to make this smooth?
Nora (People Ops): Upload spouses job offer or HR benefits letter with effective date to benefits portal -> Manage Dependents -> Change Dependent Coverage. Use filename: eli-marshall-spouse-newjob.pdf. Add a short note: "Dropping spouse due to new employer coverage effective 2025-11-01".
PayrollBot: Ticket created: PAY-8243. Payroll adjustment queued pending People Ops & Benefits confirmation.
Eli (Eng): If spouse enrolls with their employer but coverage start is retroactive (e.g., employer applies coverage to first of month but hiring date is mid-month), which date do we use?
Kai (Benefits): We use the carrier-accepted effective date on their benefits confirmation. If their employer lists 11/1 as effective, that will be the QLE effective date even if payroll deductions start later. If there's ambiguity, upload the carrier letter and well confirm.
Eli (Eng): Suppose spouse keeps our plan and their new employer also covers them for a month while waiting for benefits onboarding. Any advice on coordination of benefits?
Kai (Benefits): Dual coverage can complicate claims. Typically one plan is primary (usually the employees own employer), the other secondary. Coordination of benefits determines who pays first. If you anticipate overlap, keep both active until primary coverage is confirmed, or coordinate with spouses HR to get clear effective dates. Filing claims with both carriers might be needed.
Eli (Eng): Understood. Ill upload the HR letter now. Thanks everyone :v:
